purpose: Unapproved branding direction, not a screenshot of implemented software
prompt:
Generate one exceptional high-fidelity desktop app UI concept for TENET, a local read-only inspector of coding-agent policy decisions. Landscape 1536x1024, actual application edge to edge, not a laptop or moodboard. This is concept 2, 'Trace studio'. Give it a wholly committed contemporary professional creative-software identity: matte deep plum #292433 and dusty aubergine #43384F for the surrounding workspace, a broad pale lilac #F3EEF8 reading plane, carefully placed lavender #D5C7F0 navigation selection and muted peach accents. This is NOT a black-and-neon cyberpunk dashboard. No glow, glass, gradients, floating glass cards, decorative graph squiggles or purple marketing hero. Crisp neutral humanist sans text, clear code typography, highly considered compact spacing, beautiful custom TENET logotype with a small abstract paired-gate mark.

Composition is a tracing workspace, not a centered article. At left a 280px matte plum navigation rail extends full height. TENET wordmark at top, 'Local archive' and a compact session selector 'tenet-observe'. A vertical chronological list of recent calls connected by a subtle hairline and small semantic status symbols. Selected row 'Shell command' and 'Would block', a restrained lavender selection plane; other rows 'Edit file / Would allow', 'Edit file / Block', 'Shell command / Would allow', 'Edit file / Would ask for approval'. Time labels are small. Dark rail footer 'Read-only'. The main area has a thin dark toolbar with 'Call summary' and 'Refresh archive'. Beneath it the pale lilac workspace occupies almost all remaining width and height, with gentle 10px outer top corners, not multiple nested cards.

The upper quarter of the reading workspace is one horizontal recorded trace: 'Shell command' at left, linked by a simple line to a dominant 'Would block' outcome, then separately to 'Ran' at right. Labels 'Action', 'TENET decision', 'Actual execution' clarify that this is recorded data, not clickable enforcement controls. Make 'Would block' the confident focal text, approximately 56px; 'Ran' deliberately smaller but unmistakable. An octagonal coral-red outlined policy symbol and a neutral checked execution symbol. Below the trace, a dark aubergine code inset with the exact command 'git status --short && git diff -- README.md && git diff --cached --stat'. Immediately after, one readable sentence 'The call ran. Observe mode records decisions without enforcing them.'

The lower workspace changes pace: a broad left reading area headed 'Why this decision', with the explanation 'Evidence confidence was below the required threshold.' Show the actual rule 'Never send any email without confirmation.' and 'Rule at line 5', plus a small green outcome chip 'PASS'. To its right, aligned as a compact but readable diagnostic region, a high-quality exact linear confidence meter labeled 'Evidence confidence', 'Recorded 0.85', 'Required 0.9'. Meter goes from 0 to 1, amber fill exactly 85% and a thin dark threshold marker at 90%. This is NOT a circular health score or arbitrary progress bar. Below rule and meter, the clarification 'PASS is not a reported violation. The evidence-confidence check did not pass.' Lower still, aligned understated disclosure rows 'Submitted questions', 'Shared evidence', 'All rules', 'Recording details', with restrained chevrons and hairline separators. Bottom status text 'Synthetic preview data'. Use a complete coherent system across wordmark, navigation, icons, labels, state symbols and controls. The screen should feel like a serious, beautifully designed developer studio with useful density and breathing room in intentional places. Do not invent approvals, guarantees, latency numbers, enforcement switches, charts or product features. One refined screen only.
reviewNotes: Branding reference only. Numeric meter geometry and semantic status colors require exact implementation rather than copying generated pixels.
